definitions.explanation: Treating someone or something better than others, often through special benefits, privileges, or consideration. Used as a suru verb.

examples.japanese: {社員|しゃいん}を{優遇|ゆうぐう}する。
この{会社|かいしゃ}は{子育|こそだ}て{中|ちゅう}の{社員|しゃいん}を{優遇|ゆうぐう}している。
examples.english: This company gives preferential treatment to employees raising children.

examples.japanese: {税制|ぜいせい}の{優遇|ゆうぐう}{措置|そち}を{受|う}けるために{申請|しんせい}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: An application is required to receive preferential tax treatment.

notes:
USAGE:
Commonly used in business, government policy, and employment contexts. Often appears in discussions of tax benefits, employee benefits, and social welfare programs.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {優遇|ゆうぐう}する (to give preferential treatment)
- {優遇|ゆうぐう}{措置|そち} (preferential measures)
- {優遇|ゆうぐう}{税制|ぜいせい} (preferential tax system)
- {優遇|ゆうぐう}{金利|きんり} (preferential interest rate)

CONTRAST:
- {冷遇|れいぐう}: cold treatment, neglect — the opposite of {優遇|ゆうぐう}
